title: Routing-rule exegesis and heuristic synthesis for safe fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Refactor the policy intake and validation layer to provide an interpretable semantics (exegesis) of routing rules and a fast heuristic synthesis path for safe fallbacks. Current policy compiler rejects many legitimate progressive-rollout rules and fails to produce succinct fallback candidates for unavailable model variants. This ticket delivers: (1) a deterministic rule normalizer that produces a canonical AST annotated with provenance; (2) a lightweight heuristic synthesizer that proposes fallback model variants and region-tier downgrades with safety scores; (3) a validation harness that emits human-readable explanations and autofix suggestions for common misconfigurations; and (4) backwards-compatible migration shims for existing routing configs.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical normalizer produces identical canonical AST for semantically-equivalent rules (unit test coverage >= 95%).
Heuristic synthesizer returns fallback candidates within 30ms P95 for typical policy size (<= 25 rules).
Validation harness surfaces clear explanations for failures and suggests an autofix in >= 70% of common cases observed in telemetry.
No behavioral regressions for existing e2e routing tests across hosted/dedicated/private modes.
Migration shim can translate 99% of existing customer configs without manual edits; remaining cases generate actionable diagnostics.
Security review completed and signed off by Security team.
Feature gated behind runtime-1.24 flag and toggleable per-tenant via Console.
implementation_notes: Split into two packages: policy-exegesis (canonicalizer + explainers) and fallback-synthesizer (heuristic ranking + safety scoring).
Canonicalizer normalizes order-insensitive constructs, hoists common predicates, and emits provenance metadata as annotations (string tags in AST).

Fallback synthesizer uses a heuristic priority list: exact model variant -> compatible quantized variant -> regional equivalent -> lower-tier model; each candidate is scored by latency delta, cost delta, and semantic distance (string metric on model names).
Expose an ambiguity-level metric (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH) in validation output to guide reviewers during canary rollouts.
Add metrics: validation_error_rate, autofix_applied_rate, synth_latency_ms_p95, synth_candidate_count.
Keep the old policy compiler as a fallback path behind a runtime toggle for 2 releases to allow gradual migration.
migration_plan: Phase 1: deploy canonicalizer + explainers behind feature flag and run in dry-run mode on traffic for 2 weeks. Phase 2: enable fallback-synthesizer for internal customers and collect telemetry. Phase 3: enable autofix suggestions in Console for admins. Phase 4: enable automatic migration for low-risk configs in release runtime-1.25. Provide a migration dashboard showing diffs and flagged configs.
risks: False-positive autofixes could change customer behavior—mitigation: require admin approval for any automated change and run extensive unit & canary tests.
Performance regression of policy intake pipeline—mitigation: microbenchmarks and P95 latency target of 5ms for validation call in the hot path, otherwise revert to legacy path.
Edge cases where heuristic synthesizer suggests semantically incompatible fallbacks—mitigation: include semantic distance check and conservative safety threshold defaulted to HIGH.
Migration complexity for very large or hand-optimized rule sets—mitigation: provide migration reports and a manual rollback path.
test_plan: Unit tests for canonicalizer equivalence classes and provable invariants.
Property tests that generate random routing rules and assert normalization idempotence.
Benchmarks for synthesizer latency and candidate quality on representative production traces.
Integration tests: simulate regional outage and assert synthesized fallback keeps SLOs for latency and cost within expected bounds.
User acceptance: Console display of validation explanations validated by PM and Design for clarity.
